normative_extracts.quote: The accessibility tree is a subset of the DOM tree exposed to platform accessibility APIs (UIA, NSAccessibility, ATK) containing each node's computed Role, Accessible Name, Description, and States.

pipeline_phases: Platform A11y IPC Tree (UIA / AX / ATK)
engine_internals.mechanism_summary: The browser builds a parallel Accessibility Tree from semantic HTML and ARIA attributes, filtering display:none/aria-hidden nodes and computing Accessible Names for OS screen readers.

production_failures.symptom: Clickable <div onclick> button is invisible to keyboard Tab and announced as plain text by screen readers
production_failures.root_cause: Adding role='button' alone exposes the ARIA role without keyboard focusability (tabindex='0') or Enter/Space activation.
production_failures.mitigation: Use native <button type='button'>, which provides role, tabindex, Enter/Space handlers, and disabled state automatically.

production_failures.symptom: aria-hidden='true' placed on a modal's ancestor traps screen reader users in silence while focus sits inside
production_failures.root_cause: Putting aria-hidden='true' on a focusable element or its ancestor hides it from the accessibility tree while leaving it in the keyboard Tab order.
production_failures.mitigation: Use native <dialog>.showModal() or the HTML inert attribute to hide background subtrees from both focus and the accessibility tree.
